title: Using TypeScript in a Development Workflow knowledge check

questions.prompt: What is the role of TypeScript in a development workflow?
options: It removes the need for runtime tests.
It checks types and improves tooling; the application still runs as JavaScript in its selected runtime.
It replaces the JavaScript runtime in every browser.
It validates all network data automatically.
questions.answer_key: It checks types and improves tooling; the application still runs as JavaScript in its selected runtime.
questions.explanation: Type checking is a development-time layer and does not replace runtime verification.

questions.prompt: Which statement is correct about “Using TypeScript in a Development Workflow”?
options: The concept should be demonstrated with editor diagnostics and autocomplete and checked against its intended contract.
The safest approach is to skip diagnostics and trust the first output.
A type assertion automatically validates every value at runtime.
The learner should publish hidden solutions so the exercise can grade itself.
questions.answer_key: The concept should be demonstrated with editor diagnostics and autocomplete and checked against its intended contract.
questions.explanation: The supplied syllabus explicitly includes “Editor diagnostics and autocomplete”; connect it to a concrete example and verify the behavior relevant to this lesson.

questions.prompt: What is a good verification step after practicing “Using TypeScript in a Development Workflow”?
options: Assume separating type checking, building, and running code is unnecessary because the code has type annotations.
Ignore compiler or test failures if the interface looks correct.
Treat passing a static token check as proof that the program executed correctly.
Check compiler watch mode, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
questions.answer_key: Check compiler watch mode, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
questions.explanation: The syllabus includes “Compiler watch mode”. Verification should match the concept: type-level checks, runtime tests, configuration checks or human review as appropriate.
